clauses: alien selection

starting hand size
first player selection
answers.answer: Aliens are selected by shuffling cosmic combo cards, revealing the top, gathering the indicated sheets, and dealing one randomly to each player. The cosmic deck uses encounter, reinforcement, and artifact cards; this summary does not say that flares enter it. Each player receives 8 cards. In the first game the youngest player starts; later, reveal destiny cards until one shows a player's color, and that player starts.

clauses: what counts as one colony
whether several players can have colonies on one planet
whether five foreign colonies must be in different systems
answers.answer: The summary identifies colonies as colonies on planets outside a player's home system and says an offense win establishes a colony on the targeted planet. It does not define the exact counting unit, whether multiple players can simultaneously have colonies on one planet, or whether the five must occupy different systems; those details are unsupported here.

evidence.heading: Overview
evidence.quote: Cosmic Encounter is a social negotiation and hand-management game where each player is a unique alien species attempting to colonize foreign planets. Players use diplomacy, alliances, and force to establish colonies outside their home system. The first player to have 5 foreign colonies wins. If multiple players reach 5 foreign colonies simultaneously, they share the victory.

evidence.heading: Winning an Encounter (Offense)
evidence.quote: **Winning an Encounter (Offense):** Offense and allied ships land on the targeted planet, establishing colonies.

evidence.heading: Scoring / Victory Conditions
evidence.quote:
- The first player to have 5 foreign colonies (colonies on planets outside their home system) wins.
- If multiple players reach 5 foreign colonies at the same time, they share the victory.
- Colony markers on the Warp track help track each player's foreign colony count.

answers.answer: Offense totals 10 + 6 = 16; defense totals 12 + 4 = 16. Ties go to defense. Offense and offensive allies go to the Warp; defense ships remain; defensive allies receive defender rewards. The summary does not specify what happens to bystander ships/colonies in this case.

evidence.heading: Actions — Attack Cards
evidence.quote: - **Attack Cards (value 00-40):** Each side totals their attack card value + number of their ships (including allies). Higher total wins. Ties go to the defense.

evidence.heading: Winning an Encounter (Defense)
evidence.quote: **Winning an Encounter (Defense):** Offense and allied ships go to the Warp. Defense ships remain. Defensive allies receive defender rewards (draw 1 card from deck or retrieve 1 ship from Warp per ship committed).

clauses: offense without encounter cards at Start Turn
defense without encounter cards at Planning
offense losing its last encounter card later
whether other cards must be played before replacement
answers.answer: At Start Turn, an offense with no encounter cards discards its hand and draws 8, repeating until it has an encounter card. A defense without encounter cards when required reveals and discards its remaining hand and draws 8, repeating until it has one. If offense runs out before Planning because of a power or card effect, its turn ends immediately and all committed ships return to colonies. The summary does not say that other cards must be played before replacement.

evidence.heading: Turn Structure — Start Turn
evidence.quote: 1. **Start Turn:** If the offense has no encounter cards, discard hand and draw 8 new cards; repeat until they have at least one encounter card.

evidence.heading: Special Rules & Edge Cases — Empty Hand (Offense and Defense)
evidence.quote: - **Empty Hand (Offense):** If the offense has no encounter cards at the Start Turn phase, they discard their hand and draw 8 new cards, repeating until they have an encounter card. If the offense runs out of encounter cards before Planning (due to alien power or card effect), their turn ends immediately and all committed ships return to colonies. **Empty Hand (Defense):** If the defense has no encounter cards when they must play one, they reveal their remaining hand, discard it, and draw 8 new cards, repeating until they have an encounter card.

It says running out before Planning due to a power or card effect ends the turn and returns committed ships; otherwise it does not separately describe ordinary turn termination after the first loss or after the second encounter.

evidence.heading: Turn Structure — second encounter

clauses: exact home-colony thresholds for losing and regaining power

answers.answer: The summary says losing all ships from a home planet loses that colony; having fewer than three home colonies removes the alien power, and reaching three or more restores it immediately. It does not say whether a power can be used one last time upon loss. Cosmic Zap cancels one use of an alien power and prevents that power from being used again for the rest of the current encounter; whether that covers every printed part of a multi-part sheet is not specified.

evidence.heading: Special Rules & Edge Cases — Home System Defense
evidence.quote: - **Home System Defense:** If you lose all ships from a home planet, you lose that colony. If you ever have fewer than three home colonies, you lose your alien power; you regain it immediately if you reach three or more home colonies again.

evidence.heading: Special Rules & Edge Cases — Cosmic Zap
evidence.quote: - **Cosmic Zap:** An artifact that cancels one use of any alien's power (including your own). That power cannot be used again for the rest of the current encounter.
